answer: Behavioral kernel divergence scoring. Each agent identity's transaction kernel (timing, amount, counterparty mix) is embedded; post-hoc, identities whose kernels cluster too tightly are flagged as one operator. The rule: flagged clusters lose accumulated reputation and future payouts. This forces attackers to make each identity's kernel genuinely distinct, costing real per-identity operational divergence—separate dune of behavior—rather than cheap duplication. A crystal of shared history becomes the tell.
